title: Young's double slit; Stationary waves and harmonics
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for OCR A-level (A) Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: W07-uk1#t1 term and clue written for the game; W10-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; W07-uk1#t4 term and clue written for the game; W10-1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: W10-1#N.4a, W10-uk1#N.6, W10-1#N.8a, W10-uk1#N.8, W10-uk1#N.10.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Travelling microscope
items.clue: Instrument used to measure the separation of the two slits directly.

items.label: Node
items.clue: Point where the amplitude is zero at all times; the next one is λ/2 away.

items.label: Laser
items.clue: Monochromatic, coherent source used in a darkened room, with its own safety rules.

items.label: Reflection
items.clue: Bouncing back from a fixed end or pipe end, which supplies the partner moving the opposite way.

questions.stem: A string fixed at both ends vibrates in a standing wave. Its nodes are at x = 0, 0.40 m, 0.80 m and 1.20 m, measured from one end. Points P, Q and R on the string are at x = 0.10 m, 0.20 m and 0.70 m. Which statement about the oscillations of P, Q and R is correct?

options.text: P and Q oscillate π/4 rad out of phase, being λ/8 apart.
P and Q oscillate in phase, with amplitudes equal to each other.
P and R oscillate in antiphase, with equal amplitudes.
P and R oscillate in phase, with equal amplitudes.

questions.stem: A tuning fork of frequency 384 Hz is held over a resonance tube. The first resonance occurs when the air column is 22.0 cm long. Ignoring any end correction, what is the speed of sound in the air?
questions.explanation: First resonance: L = λ/4, so λ = 4 × 0.220 = 0.880 m. v = fλ = 384 × 0.880 = 338 m s⁻¹.

questions.stem: A pipe of length 0.68 m is closed at one end and open at the other. The speed of sound in the air in the pipe is 340 m s⁻¹. Which gives, in increasing order, the lowest frequencies at which the air in the pipe resonates?
A probe is moved between a microwave transmitter and a metal reflector. Adjacent minima of the received signal are 1.5 cm apart. What is the frequency of the microwaves?
questions.explanation: Node to node = λ/2, so λ = 3.0 cm. f = c/λ = 3.00 × 10⁸ ÷ 0.030 = 1.0 × 10¹⁰ Hz.

questions.stem: A loudspeaker emitting a 1000 Hz note faces a hard wall. A microphone moved along the line between them detects positions of minimum loudness 0.17 m apart. What is the speed of sound?
questions.explanation: Node to node = λ/2, so λ = 0.34 m. v = fλ = 1000 × 0.34 = 340 m s⁻¹.
